pairs: Et vidi alium angelum fortem descendentem de cælo amictum nube,
And I saw another strong Angel, descending from heaven, clothed with a cloud.
et iris in capite ejus,
And a rainbow was upon his head,
et facies ejus erat ut sol,
and his face was like the sun,
et pedes ejus tamquam columnæ ignis:
and his feet were like columns of fire.
et habebat in manu sua libellum apertum:
And he held in his hand a small open book.
et posuit pedem suum dextrum super mare,
And he stationed his right foot upon the sea,
sinistrum autem super terram:
and his left foot upon the land.
et clamavit voce magna,
And he cried out with a great voice,
quemadmodum cum leo rugit.
in the manner of a lion roaring.
Et cum clamasset,
And when he had cried out,
locuta sunt septem tonitrua voces suas.
seven thunders uttered their voices.
Et cum locuta fuissent septem tonitrua voces suas,
And when the seven thunders had uttered their voices,
ego scripturus eram:
I was about to write.
et audivi vocem de cælo dicentem mihi:
But I heard a voice from heaven, saying to me:
Signa quæ locuta sunt septem tonitrua:
“Seal the things that the seven thunders have spoken,
et noli ea scribere.
and do not write them.”
Et angelus,
And the Angel,
quem vidi stantem super mare et super terram,
whom I saw standing upon the sea and upon the land,
levavit manum suam ad cælum:
lifted up his hand toward heaven.
et juravit per viventem in sæcula sæculorum,
And he swore by the One who lives forever and ever,
qui creavit cælum,
who created heaven,
et ea quæ in eo sunt:
and the things that are in it;
et terram,
and the earth,
et ea quæ in ea sunt:
and the things that are in it;
et mare,
and the sea,
et ea quæ in eo sunt:
and the things that are in it:
Quia tempus non erit amplius:
that the time will not be any longer,
sed in diebus vocis septimi angeli,
but in the days of the voice of the seventh Angel,
cum cœperit tuba canere,
when he shall begin to sound the trumpet,
consummabitur mysterium Dei sicut evangelizavit per servos suos prophetas.
the mystery of God will be completed, just as he has proclaimed in the Gospel, through his servants the Prophets.
Et audivi vocem de cælo iterum loquentem mecum, et dicentem:
And again, I heard a voice from heaven speaking with me and saying:
Vade, et accipe librum apertum de manu angeli stantis super mare, et super terram.
“Go and receive the open book from the hand of the Angel who stands upon the sea and upon the land.”
Et abii ad angelum,
And I went to the Angel,
dicens ei, ut daret mihi librum.
saying to him that he should give the book to me.
Et dixit mihi:
And he said to me:
Accipe librum, et devora illum:
“Receive the book and consume it.
et faciet amaricari ventrem tuum,
And it shall cause bitterness in your stomach,
sed in ore tuo erit dulce tamquam mel.
but in your mouth it shall be sweet like honey.”
Et accepi librum de manu angeli,
And I received the book from the hand of the Angel,
et devoravi illum:
and I consumed it.
et erat in ore meo tamquam mel dulce,
And it was sweet like honey in my mouth.
et cum devorassem eum,
And when I had consumed it,
amaricatus est venter meus:
my stomach was made bitter.
et dixit mihi:
And he said to me,
Oportet te iterum prophetare gentibus,
“It is necessary for you to prophesy again about many nations
et populis,
and peoples
et linguis,
and languages
et regibus multis.
and kings.”
